name: Publication Management
description: Seven-screen internal editorial workspace for small biotech research teams: versioned manuscript stages, coauthor approvals, review decisions, source-verified journal/congress targets, submission history and evidence-backed progress reports.
whenToUse: Research teams with fewer than 50 people needing a lightweight way to plan manuscripts/posters, coordinate author and reviewer decisions, preserve timelines, and report journal submission state manually.
whenNotToUse: Not a journal submission system, collaborative word processor, author identity portal, patient data store, GxP-certified signature platform or commercial publication compliance/impact analytics suite.

instructions: Read the current TrialAgents authoring and usage guidance (1.3.9 or newer) and live design kit. This is Publication Management, an internal TrialAgents app for small biotech and research teams (<50 FTE), based conceptually on iEnvision Datavision planning, review and reporting. NO app auth/accounts or invented TrialAgents logo; use the official host watermark linked to https://platform.trialagents.com. Keep seven distinctive screens and one title plus one subline per screen. The sidebar name "Publication Management" must display in full without an icon. Never create external journal integrations, journal submissions, signatures, patient data or proprietary citation analytics. Before creation, read the available real schema and catalog, then prepare exactly eight authorized scalar tables: projects, manuscripts, authors, reviews, targets, milestones, submissions, reports. Map each logical field to the real lowercase physical key and include it in the manifest with the real table ID, schemaVersion, read/write mode and allowed fields. Use the returned reviewed parent record IDs when linking children. No demo data may enter production. Host injects templateConfiguration and templateBindings: do not prepend them in catalog source. Native layout uses templateLayoutSchema, heading and layoutProfile; gear emits tracker:layout, and changes persist only after prepare_tool_layout review. Forms use data-ui-state on every input, select and textarea and named event.form fields. records.propose is only a proposal; confirm in the host and reconcile original optimistic record versions, never mark saved before receipt. All source reads must prove completeness; handle denied, partial, unknown total and over-budget as missing coverage. Allow all relevant record roles to create/edit/duplicate/archive with protected historical states reset on duplicate, and reachable pagination. Manuscript status Submitted requires existing dated confirmation, current-version author acceptances/disclosures and approved reviews plus source-verified outlet. Published additionally requires actual published event and DOI/date; do not infer from target dates. Store original target/baseline dates immutably, and retain distinct revisions. Author approvals are per draft version, not transferable. Independent database changes are not protected by UI checks: never claim enforced foreign keys. Saved reports are human reviewed, source-identified, versioned and never automatically mailed. ChatGPT drafting and optional public outlet-requirement research happen only through the shared authorized TrialAgents runner; TrialAgents handles any separately approved email. Save the app first; optional automation configuration must not block it. No automation is enabled by this catalog. Do not invent a per-app ChatGPT Task, active subscription or outgoing message. Tests in standalone browser are not live host acceptance; verify the sanitized frame, real QuickJS, manifest, database and catalog discovery before publishing. Keep one main heading/subline, rich editorial styling, responsive 320-1440 layouts. Preserve same app ID on revisions and never create replacement apps after ambiguous receipts. Discover with list_app_templates, read_app_template and the exact current digest, then prepare_app_from_template. Reuse suitable authorized tables. For preview corrections use replacesPreviewId and expectedDigest with the same requestKey; for saved revisions read_project_component and retain its component ID and current version. After native layout confirmation use read_project_component(includeOutput:true). Withdrawn requires a separately recorded dated withdrawal confirmation; historical submission/withdrawal evidence remains protected.

quickStart: Open the internal TrialAgents project and create Publication Management using the exact catalog id/version. No second login, author portal or branded in-app icon.

Read the project and existing authorized database table schemas. Prepare eight scalar role tables using dataContract field kinds and selected options; create parents first, then link child records using reviewed receipt UUIDs.

Configure tableMap with real table IDs, physical column keys and allowed writable logical fields. Declare every bound read/write field in the versioned manifest and check access before opening the app.
Enter actual manuscript versions, author roles, review decisions, target source links, milestones and submission records. Do not seed fictional examples.
Use the host gear for native Layout; confirm reviewed changes and reopen the same app ID/version. No special auth or automation setup is required for ordinary use.
Optionally set up ChatGPT or email actions from the existing TrialAgents Automations page only after the app has been saved and the scope is approved.

documentation.dataContract: Eight scalar role tables (projects, manuscripts, authors, reviews, targets, milestones, submissions, reports). All fields use lowercase underscore physical keys, with exact logical-to-physical mappings in tableMap. Every scalar has multiple:false, select fields have enumerated options. Required parent IDs are text UUID references to saved authorized records; never use relationships/arrays as IDs. Schema kinds and physical keys: projects: name (text), objective (text), lead (text), archived (boolean); manuscripts: name (text), project_id (text), type (select), status (select), version_label (text), lead (text), target_id (text), target_date (date), initial_target (date), source_url (text), next_action (text), submitted_at (date), published_at (date), doi (text), archived (boolean); authors: name (text), manuscript_id (text), affiliation (text), contribution (text), order (number), invited (boolean), declaration (select), approval (select), approved_version (text), approved_at (date), notes (text), archived (boolean); reviews: name (text), manuscript_id (text), draft_version (text), reviewer (text), feedback_type (select), status (select), due (date), reviewed_at (date), resolved_at (date), approved_at (date), action (text), notes (text), archived (boolean); targets: name (text), kind (select), category (text), scope (text), url (text), verified_at (date), deadline (date), original_deadline (date), alternative (text), notes (text), archived (boolean); milestones: name (text), manuscript_id (text), phase (select), baseline (date), due (date), actual_at (date), owner (text), status (select), notes (text), archived (boolean); submissions: name (text), manuscript_id (text), kind (select), at (date), decision (select), confirmation (text), source_url (text), doi (text), notes (text), archived (boolean); reports: name (text), project_id (text), period (date), cutoff (date), status (select), owner (text), approved_at (date), references (text), body (text), risks (text), archived (boolean). All source URLs, evidence text, notes and report narratives are database text. Date fields are ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Empty optional dates are null; missing required fields must not be coerced into success. Archived is a boolean and requires reviewed update. The app never creates users, passwords, external author accounts or auth tables. Custom frontend-js is app-level access: hiding a tab is never an access grant. The host supplies account, permissions, audit and official linked watermark. Set tableMap to a JSON string {role:{typeId:actual saved UUID,fields:{logicalKey:physical_key},writableFields:[authorized logical keys]}}. Use the eight complete schemas in quickStart with multiple:false; optional blank dates/numbers are null. Create projects/targets first, then manuscripts, then children; use committed receipt UUIDs, including report references. Every readable field must be mapped with current schemaVersion/kind/mode; missing mappings and array values are incomplete. Reads/search cover at most 1200 records per role; use a smaller complete authorized dataset beyond that limit. Evidence checks are application logic, not database-wide integrity constraints.
documentation.interactionContract: One H1 and subline per view, seven unique publication workspaces with native tracker:layout. Every transient input/select/textarea has data-ui-state and stable data-action/name. The host injects templateConfiguration and templateBindings exactly once. All database reads use declared typeIds/fields, bounded paging and completeness checks. No count/zero/approval claim on denied/partial/unknown-total data. Tables/boards have reachable pagination; create/edit/duplicate/archive generate exact records.propose operations and carry original expectedVersion through confirmation. Draft input is preserved on errors. Hidden presentation columns remain editable in the details form. Selected project filters are applied before calculating metrics. Submission, publication and report approval require source-backed evidence; statuses are not sent to journals. App-level access is inherited from TrialAgents; custom tabs are not separate security boundaries. Official watermark/link are supplied by host. Platform Automations alone manages optional tasks. Validation and stale-version messages appear inside open forms. Proposals retain drafts until host confirmation/reopen. Native field order/visibility controls registers and editor fields; Additional fields keeps hidden required inputs reachable. Submission history is paged. Copied drafts have no original record identity. Source URLs open through the trusted host link adapter.
documentation.lifecycle: Publication records use stable UUIDs and append evidence per draft and submission; the baseline deadline and original source are retained. Changing draft version does not transplant author/review approval. Copies reset version-specific approval and submission/output status, never create new app accounts. Archive checks dependent author, review, milestone, event and reporting roles with complete authorized reads; reviewed reports cannot be archived without returning to Draft. There are no database foreign keys enforced by this source. Config changes are reviewed with expected app version; keep IDs, bindings, audit, grants and disabled automation state across revisions. Saved app remains usable if optional automation or email fails. Reconcile ambiguous save receipts and avoid duplicating proposed writes. Use one requestKey for initial preparation and reconcile the same receipt after ambiguity. Revisions target the same component ID and expectedVersion; do not create replacement apps to recover. Never resubmit a retained create draft after ambiguous confirmation without receipt reconciliation. Standalone preview is fictional only. asOf is a date-comparison reference, not a historical snapshot.
limitations: Offline preview uses fictional journal titles, URLs, people and DOIs, never real records, journal submissions, automated correspondence or citations.
No native journal portal, publisher API, electronic signature, compliance certification, impact factor, citation analytics or full-text storage.
Custom-app screen visibility is not independent authorization; TrialAgents host enforces app/table/field/record access.

The standalone fictional preview alone does not prove production integration. QA.md records actual QuickJS, sanitized frame, database, design and native layout checks. Live deployed MCP discovery, connected ChatGPT acceptance and actual scheduled runs/delivery are separate checks.
Complete historical source coverage depends on bounded reads and real table permissions. When incomplete, overview/review claims are withheld.
Task guidance is optional metadata and never enables automations or email without separate reviewed approval.

examples.prompt: Create Publication Management for a five-person biotech editorial team. Set up eight scalar tables and bind manuscript, author, review, outlet, submission and report records using real saved UUIDs. No example data.
examples.expectedBehavior: Read host schemas, create reviewed tables and records, map physical keys and show seven empty/useful screens with platform access, native layout settings and no app login.

examples.prompt: Record author responses for manuscript version v3 and prepare submission.
examples.expectedBehavior: Return reviewed proposals. Verify current-version author acceptances, disclosures, approved review rounds and verified target requirements; refuse Submitted until an actual dated submission event with confirmation exists.

examples.prompt: Prepare a publication update report through the end of October using only recorded evidence.
examples.expectedBehavior: Generate a draft with exact source manuscript IDs, known gaps and limitations; save only after human review; no invented submission/DOI/impact factor and no external communication.

examples.prompt: Compare journal options and keep deadlines source-dated.
examples.expectedBehavior: Use public official sources when authorized, record verified URLs and original/current deadlines as reviewed proposals; flag inaccessible or stale instructions instead of guessing.

examples.prompt: Offer optional weekly publication status review, and notify the owner only if separately approved.
examples.expectedBehavior: Save the app independently; configure one shared-runner monitor in TrialAgents only with explicit owner approval, scope and coverage, and a separately approved backend email action with fixed safe text; never report an automation as active merely from this template.

tasks.whenUseful: Use when a small CRO or biotech team wants a periodic internal publication progress review, a source-dated public outlet requirements check, or separate authorized team-only email after an approved evidence-linked report. No automation is needed for normal tracking.
tasks.readRequirements: Save app first. Choose explicitly authorized projects and fields. Research source list: verified official journal/congress websites and approved manuscript/author/review/event records. Trigger suggestion weekly Europe/Berlin or a specific database state change; source cutoff and deduplication by actual manuscript UUID + draft version + report period. Read every relevant role to complete coverage; on inaccessible sources yield partial, no claimed completion; do not infer author acceptance from text. Standing writes only if separately approved and scoped with expiry/limits. TrialAgents user account and app permissions remain authoritative. Use stable authoringKey publication_progress_review_v1 for research and publication_reviewed_report_email_v1 for email. Check read_automation_setup and current guide, reuse existing IDs/versions, owner-confirmed IANA timezone and weekly anchor, approved expiry and current scopes. No host setup means pending, not active. Manual review remains available. Suggested weekly review Monday 09:00 in the owner-confirmed IANA timezone, with an approved anchor and expiry. Prefer a supported Work chat, high reasoning and the latest most capable model in the owner subscription; these are preferences, not verified host execution settings or invented tool parameters. Use prepare_app_monitoring for research and prepare_app_action for the independent email rule; inspect list_app_automations/read_app_automation before creation.
tasks.outputContract: Save proposed reviewed report to existing reports table with source manuscript IDs, period, cutoff, exclusions, author, status Draft. Successful saved receipts must be reconciled, and approval separately reviewed. No new approved evidence yields a documented no-change result; do not use no_update as quiet mode unless coverage is complete and the owner explicitly approves silence. Separate TrialAgents email if requested: use fixed text such as "An approved Publication Management report is available in TrialAgents.", send to owner and approved existing teammates only; never unsupported placeholders or email from ChatGPT. Partial failures leave tracking app intact. Fixed email subject: Publication report reviewed. Fixed body: Open https://platform.trialagents.com to review your authorized publication report. Use a separate single-step database transition into reports.status=Reviewed, declare mapped status/archived fields and recheck archived is not true. Registered owner and explicitly selected app-authorized team only. No duplicate completion email, digest mode or subdaily email schedule. Preserve disabled state and hidden settings on edits. Archive suspends work; restore/copy does not activate it. Delivery failure never reruns successful research; outcomes belong in Logs. Ordinary manual use needs no runner, monitor, mail action or external account. If setup is unavailable or declined, keep the app saved and use the prompt on demand. Keep definitions editable when disabled; no standalone automation Delete action.
